Sendai Yuusha wa Inkyou Shitai

The Previous Hero wants to Retire

Chapter 56 - The Preceding Hero and the Morning That Came Again

Synopsis

The slightly lewd middle school student, Yashiro Yuu, was summoned to a different world in the summer break of his second year of middle school! It was a fantasy world of swords and magic! Fighting for the sake of the cute princess that summoned him, he, who occasionally got setback but nevertheless continued to fight as long as he still had life in him, finally brought peace to the world! ―――― Three years after that, the Demon Lord that the Preceding Hero should have defeated is revived, and the world has once again been wrapped in chaos. At that time, four new Heroes have been summoned!

For the sake of bringing peace to the world, the Second Generation Hero, Amagi Kaito draws his sword!

………………But, they didn’t know. That the male high school student that had no Maryoku (magical power) whatsoever that was summoned together with Amagi Kaito and the others was actually the Preceding Hero that defeated the Demon Lord three years ago―――!!

But however, the Preceding Hero didn’t get involved with them. After all, he totally wanted to fully enjoy this other world~.

This is the ‘being true to his own desires but still looking like he’ll save the world again in the end’ Hero’s, Yashiro Yuu’s heartwarming fantasy life!

What do you do?

Location: a mid sized city in America

Time: Winter (snowy)

Zombie Type: Walking Dead
You find yourself in the midst of a zombie outbreak...

I'll take advantage of the snow, since zombies don't produce body heat they'll freeze. The other people in the city will probably be more of a problem. I'll try to get all the food I can get that won't expire, a lighter, and an axe, and then hussle outta there on a mountain bike and head for the wilderness. I don't have any guns, so the axe will have to do as a weapon, and I can also use it to chop down trees for fire.

Get my backpacking gear together and walk north.

Walking dead zombies are very similar to the shambling romero zombies, so anyone with basic cardio could outpace them.

I don't think out running from them is a problem, there are other problems. What if you find yourself in the path of a horde? The scary thing about these kinds of zombies is that they are the equivalent of an unstoppable force.

Would you go by yourself?

True, but if the situation is a US city during the winter months, snow an ice are loud and hard to traverse, even for a human. I would expect a horde to make quite a bit of noise, and that's assuming they aren't already frozen in place. Assuming theres snow around, I wouldn't be worried about them sneaking up on me, even when asleep. When awake, I can outpace them, so making snow-noise is not so much an issue in my mind (expect in the scenario of other humans wishing to do me harm). I'm assuming a more northern city in this case.

If the situation involved, say, a small new mexico town, I'd probably go high-mobility. Wait out the initial chaos (human and walker alike) then find an enduro-bike from a dealership or off a trailer somewhere. Open freeway travel is pretty fast, even in gridlock traffic one can maneuver. Gas should still be readily available if we are amusing the living to dead ratio of TWD tv show. I'd estimate it would take 3-4 days to get to the Canadian border, by way of a rocky mtn route through montana or idaho, requiring 2-3 fuel stops, and 2 nights in the open before I hit the snowline and the walkers freeze up.

I would bring family along if they were already with me, but nobody else. Smallest footprint is safest.
The thing is they don't have to stop.

Depending on the time, rob a walmart gun section first, then take as much food as I can get and hole up in my apartment. If I got lucky, I'd take a few generators and make a gasoline trip every other week. After awhile, I could expand and make a community in my apartment building. We'd barricade doors to the staircases so that only humans could enter, and have about 30 people living together.

I think the important thing would be not to forget to have fun. Because why just survive? What's the point in living if you're doing nothing but living in fear? In that sense, I'd use a generator on a console a few times a week and play games with the community I live with.
I go to the nearest store and have a blast shopping, eating, playing games, whatever, all before I invariably die a brutal death. I just don't plan to survive a zombie outbreak.

Is this the beginning of the outbreak or after some exposure?

At the beginning, there's mass chaos. The people are as dangerous as the zombies, especially if you get between them and their supplies.

Later on, priority would be forming a small band. Not too big, but not just one or two people facing the world alone.

Then we would need to arm ourselves. Guns are heavy and noisy, although very effective. I'd shoot for everyone to have a large capacity .22 pistol and a mix of heavier 9 mm and .45 ACP pistols. One or two would need to have decent rifles, popular calibers would be best. One person needs a heavy rifle, preferably .308 to take out any vehicles or armored hostile humans. Everyone would need a hand to hand silent weapon, maybe a machete or a large knife. Crowbars, hammers, bats, or pipes would also be acceptable.

Once suitably armed, we need to find a defensible structure or build one ourselves. Even a wooden fort with palisades would be enough. Good line of sight and fresh water, preferably from a spring or well is vital.

Then, we raid and stock up on what supplies we can find. Canned goods have a long shelf life and don't need refrigeration. Anything that isn't already canned and can't be immediately eaten needs to be preserved, either by drying, fermenting, or salting.

The whole while, clearing the dead as we go would be vital. Don't leave enemies behind unless you must, don't let the concentrations increase, and don't draw attention of them and let the chase. Don't waste bullets either, armor up (rubber welcome mats would make bite proof armor) and use a spiked weapon like a pickaxe or modify a pole into a pike.

After the initial outbreak, mankind's old enemies would be worse than the walking dead. Hunger, disease, and weather would be deadly.

Location: I pick my house (located in ~100k pop. city)

First, I reorganize my neighborhood, removing all the fences between our back yards and placing them at the only 2 entrances to our neighborhood, and fencing off a small 1 acre farm behind my house, and another small one acre farm about 5 minutes walking distance away.

Then, get in the car and make a quick run to other peoples houses outside of our neighborhood and rob them, everyone else is out robbing the grocery stores; find an axe, weapons, wiring, tools, anything.

Organize parties within my neighborhood. One group takes the weapons and the axe(s) to gather some wood from a near bye 'forest' (really tiny forest, but a fuck ton of trees) and attempt to create a passage way to the river running through the forest.

Another party will be designated the task to turn every backyard and front yard into farming grounds

A third party will be designated with security within camp grounds.

See how things run for a few days / months, if successful, expand my territory to the highway, accepting all survivors who provide a tribute (membership fee) and ready the raiders. Offer all survivors / groups acceptance into my territory, and open up negations with other groups to combine our territories, but if any define a single union against the zombies, the raiders step in and take it by force.

Years pass by, my city is secure. We get functioning electricity, a small amount, but enough to power a simple AM transmitter, and we begin spreading our message of a safe society
